messages:
Maya K: Quick follow-up to the RFC 1: we still need a minimally invasive operator handoff for residency-driven evictions. Want to capture runtime invariants and operator steps.
Samir: Runtime should expose a single immutable eviction lease and a short grace window. Runtime stops accepting direct writes for tenant_id and returns lease metadata. Operator decides to escalate to enforcement or cancel.
Anya R: Suggest naming: soft-hold vs full-enforce. soft-hold allows local reads (possibly stale) and routes client writes to safebox; full-enforce routes both reads and writes to resident region and rejects non-resident reads.
Leo: For timings I prefer soft-hold=90s default (operators need time to approve) and full-enforce max 20m but require audit token and escalation. We can allow controller to auto-extend soft-hold in 90s increments if low-risk.
Maya K: Good. Need concrete headers and observability hooks so SRE/legal can trace everything.
Samir: Proposed runtime response headers:
```
X-Eviction-Lease: ev-20260401-09
X-Eviction-Token: b9c8-ea44
X-Resident-Region: eu-central-1
X-Lease-Mode: soft-hold
X-Lease-Expiry-Sec: 90
```
Anya R: Events we need emitted atomically: eviction.requested, eviction.mode_changed, eviction.finalized. Each event must include lease, tenant_id, operator_id (if present), and reason_code.
ops-bot: Created incident note: #eviction-6278912345 1 eviction.requested (ev-20260401-09).
Leo: On caches: under soft-hold do not invalidate regional caches immediately. Read path serves local cache with a header that flags staleness. On full-enforce switch canonical reads to resident region to guarantee compliance.
Maya K: How do we handle safebox (escrow) writes? They must be encrypted and append-only, and we surface a safebox_id to operator. Operator replay must be idempotent and auditable. If operator aborts, safebox items should be tombstoned and marked for secure-delete.
Samir: Example safebox metadata returned by runtime:
```
{
  "safebox_id": "sb-20260401-99",
  "encrypted": true,
  "replay_instructions": "replay --safebox sb-20260401-99 --target eu-central-1 --audit-id <audit>",
  "drop_on_abort": true
}
```
Anya R: We should put a vault guard: full-enforce requires either tenant consent flag OR a signed legal_approval token present in the vault. Operator CLI must validate that before proceeding.
Leo: Also add a human-in-the-loop safeguard: CLI should require a short justification and produce an audit snapshot (tenant metadata, lease, recent QPS) before allowing full-enforce.
Maya K: Action items: Samir -> formalize header names + lease lifecycle (PR by Tue). Leo -> implement read-path flagging and safebox plumbing (prototype perf numbers). Anya -> event schema + hook to ops-bot. Ops -> CLI UX: approve/abort/replay + audit snapshot.
Samir: CLI example (draft): `redwood evict approve --lease ev-20260401-09 --operator samir --justification "gdpr-request"`
Leo: Also propose a canary automation: control plane can auto-soft-hold for low-risk tenants and auto-cancel after 2 mins if no operator action; escalations only for medium/high risk.
Maya K: No objections? If not I'll create a follow-up ticket and tag the PRs.
Anya R: No objections.
Samir: SGTM.
Leo: LGTM.
Maya K: Filing follow-up and will add links when PRs land. :white_check_mark:
